newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market closes flat ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: NZ share market closes flat ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: * NZ top 40 index effectively up after divs stripped out
* Telecom dominates turnover
* Direction to come from FOMC meeting
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
302 -3 * NZSC cap index -8.66 at 5,040.67
290 nil * NZSE-10 cap index -2.89 at 1,099.85
322 -8 * Volume NZ$59.1 million. Futures -2 at 1101
655 +5 * Other movers - -11 -16
A sleepy New Zealand share market closed flat on Monday as most investors sat on the sidelines ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee Meeting in the United States on Tuesday.
Brokers said the market has priced in a quarter point rise in official U.S. rates.
"The market is factoring in a 25 point firming of rates but if 50 comes in then there might be a bit of a shake up," said J.B. Were and Son broker Luke Koekoek.
Whether the market would rally if the rise was limited to a quarter point was difficult to say, he said, adding that the local market was more well bid than offered.
"You might see the market edge up again but it's obviously a big week with what the Fed is doing in the U.S.," he said.
The top 40 index closed 5.85 points down at 2,223.93 but stocks shedding dividends, including Independent Newspapers and Air New Zealand, took 10.6 points off the index.
Telecom comprised almost half of the $59.1 million turnover as the first window in the company's $1 billion share buyback programme closes this week.
It closed five cents up at $6.55 on turnover of 3.9 million shares. Brokers said there was no shortage of sellers.
There was also hefty turnover in Air New Zealand "B" shares which ended 11 cents down at $3.86 after shedding an eight cent dividend.
Brokers said a large proportion of the 1.4 million shares traded was part of a portfolio.
